fable.why: Standard SDXL portrait negative list, explicitly short; well-known boilerplate any model reproduces identically.

opus.why: A focused technical question about fp8 support for a depth ControlNet. It needs accurate tooling knowledge and maybe a look at the setup, but no deep reasoning.

fable.why: Factual question about fp8 support for ControlNet depth models in the user's stack; needs accurate technical knowledge and maybe a quick web/file check, but no design work.

opus.why: A small edit to an existing Flux prompt: 1:1, no bokeh, subject on the left. It needs a little composition sense to rebalance the frame, but it's mostly mechanical.

fable.why: Mechanical edit of an existing Flux prompt (aspect, remove bokeh, reposition subject); the creative decisions were made in the earlier turn.

opus.why: Needs i2v know-how: work out why the face morphs (the orbiting camera, the smile action), rewrite as a slow push-in with stable facial wording, and add negatives. Domain judgment, but well within sonnet at high effort.

fable.why: Diagnosing i2v face morphing (orbiting camera, smile/blink triggers) and rewriting prompt plus negatives for a 5s clip needs real video-model prompt expertise; audience-facing output.

opus.why: A ComfyUI JSON edit: swap the LoRA, add a chained LoraLoader with a new ID, rewire the sampler model and both CLIP encodes, and check ID clashes. Precise wiring that haiku could get wrong.

fable.why: JSON workflow edit requiring correct rewiring of model/clip links through a new chained LoraLoader and an ID-clash check; small but easy to miswire at haiku.

opus.why: Fix the template rules that cause noun drift (enrich scenery, avoid beat words), then redo a creative prompt that must keep the domain nouns exactly. A repeat complaint, so it needs care.

fable.why: Root cause is visible in template.md (step 3/4 encourage drift and synonym swaps); fix the rule and regenerate one prompt with exact domain nouns.

opus.why: Diagnose which style words cause the doll faces, then fix with reasoning on negatives, LoRA strength, CFG and a face detailer. Visual and domain judgment, but the causes are easy to spot in the code.

fable.why: Visual diagnosis of style tokens causing doll faces, with reasoned fixes across positive, negative, LoRA strength and detailer; needs judgment but the causes are identifiable from the file.

opus.why: LoRA training diagnosis: captions with a single token, too high a dim and LR, a text-encoder LR equal to the UNet LR, too many repeats and steps. Needs solid training knowledge and a clear list of fixes.

fable.why: LoRA overfitting diagnosis (dim/alpha 128, high LR, 20 repeats, bare captions, no shuffle) requires solid training expertise and concrete parameter recommendations.

opus.why: Pipeline design for brand-mascot consistency: choosing ControlNets, IP-Adapter versus LoRA interplay, per-panel strengths, seed strategy, brand colors, all with reasoning. Architecture-level visual and brand judgment where quality matters.

fable.why: Full ComfyUI architecture for character consistency across 12 panels: controlnet/IP-adapter/LoRA stacking, per-panel strengths, seed strategy, brand-color templates with reasoning; many interacting design choices where quality drops show.
